title: Bridging Local–Global Dissonance: Learning from Compressive Measurements for Hyperspectral Reconstruction
claim: A physics-based iterative unfolding loop embeds a multi-scale encoder-decoder prior that reconciles local detail with global structure.
layout: Top unfolding chain zooms into bottom encoder-decoder; flows left-to-right, then up
description: The figure has two levels. At the top, a dashed box titled 'Deep Unfolding Framework with HSRA Prior' shows a chain of iterations. A measurement Y enters, then rotated blocks pair a teal Data Fidelity step with a purple HSRA Prior step. Dotted arrows join the iterations, and the chain ends in the reconstructed HSI. Two large green and purple arrows zoom from one iteration into a detailed bottom panel. The bottom panel is a U-shaped architecture. On the left, a salmon Encoder holds Stage 1, with MK-PTM (local sufficiency) and LWIM (latent scale) blocks feeding a Conv1x1 fusion, then Stage 2 HM-SSA and a Bottleneck HM-SSA. On the right, a grey-green Decoder holds Stage 2 HM-SSA, Stage 1 HM-SSA and a Reconstruction Block. The decoder output joins a residual sum node that yields z^(k+1), the learned prior. A gradient-step formula sits above the encoder. Blue bold labels mark the design goals.

abstract: Reconstructing hyperspectral images from compressive measurements is challenging due to a fundamental mismatch between locally reliable observations and globally entangled structures induced by spectral dispersion. This study formalizes this issue as a local–global dissonance in representation learning for CASSI systems. To resolve it, we propose a Hierarchical Scale-Reconciling Architecture (HSRA) that enforces local sufficiency and global consistency in a principled, scale-aware manner. HSRA combines multi-kernel token mixing, latent window interactions, and hierarchical multi-granularity spatially shifted attention to progressively reconcile physical constraints across scales. Embedded into a deep unfolding framework as a physically grounded learned prior, Extensive experiments on benchmarks demonstrate that HSRA achieves consistent and significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
